examples.title: Example 1: Implementing an Immersive Effect
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to use the expandSafeArea attribute to expand the safe area to the top and bottom to achieve an immersive effect.

examples.title: Example 2: Setting a Fixed Width or Height with expandSafeArea
examples.description: This example demonstrates the effect of setting both a fixed width or height and the expandSafeArea attribute.

examples.title: Example 3: Fixing the Background Image Position During Keyboard Avoidance
examples.description: This example shows how to set the expandSafeArea attribute for the background image to keep it fixed when the keyboard is displayed and the layout is adjusted.

examples.title: Example 4: Setting the Keyboard Avoidance Mode to Resize
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to use setKeyboardAvoidMode to set the keyboard avoidance mode to RESIZE, which resizes the page when the keyboard is displayed.

examples.title: Example 5: Setting Keyboard Avoidance Mode to Offset
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to use setKeyboardAvoidMode to set the keyboard avoidance mode to OFFSET, which lifts the page when the keyboard is displayed. However, if the input cursor is positioned more than the keyboard's height from the bottom of the screen, the page will not be lifted, as demonstrated in this example.

examples.title: Example 6: Switching Avoidance Modes
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to switch between OFFSET, RESIZE, and NONE modes using setKeyboardAvoidMode to achieve three different keyboard avoidance effects.

examples.title: Example 7: Expanding the Safe Area in Scrollable Containers
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to use the expandSafeArea attribute in a scrollable container to implement an immersive effect. The Swiper component in the Scroll container can extend into the status bar.

examples.title: Example 8: Extending the Component Layout Area with ignoreLayoutSafeArea
examples.description: This example shows how to use ignoreLayoutSafeArea to adjust the component position. The comparison with the default behavior (without this attribute) is as follows: After ignoreLayoutSafeArea is applied, the Row component is positioned in the upper left corner of the combined range consisting of the Stack content area, the Stack component-level safe area, and the system status bar. The component occupies the upper left portion of this expanded layout boundary.

examples.title: Example 9: Extending the Component Layout Area with ignoreLayoutSafeArea and LayoutPolicy.matchParent
examples.description: This example demonstrates how to use both ignoreLayoutSafeArea and LayoutPolicy.matchParent to adjust the component's size and position simultaneously. After ignoreLayoutSafeArea is applied, the Row component takes the lower right portion of the combined range consisting of the Stack content area and the Stack component-level safe area, and expands to fill the available space.

examples.title: Example 10: Understanding the Difference Between expandSafeArea and ignoreLayoutSafeArea
examples.description: This example demonstrates the layout effects of a container with expandSafeArea and ignoreLayoutSafeArea set, respectively, and their impact on the layout of child components. In both cases, the container visibly extends. However, the child components of the container with expandSafeArea are not affected by the container's extension, while the child components of the container with ignoreLayoutSafeArea have their positions adjusted due to the container's extension.
